letters.name: shôre ô (short a)
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'o' in 'hot' or the 'aw' in 'saw'. The default inherent vowel in Bengali consonants — every consonant carries this sound unless marked otherwise.

letters.name: shôre a (long a)
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'a' in 'father' — a long, open 'ah'. Think of opening your mouth wide like saying 'ahh' at the doctor.

letters.name: hrôshsho i (short i)
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'i' in 'bit' or 'sit'. A short, crisp 'ee' sound. Think of the dot on top like a tiny drop of ink.

letters.name: dirghô i (long i)
letters.memoryTrick: Same sound as short ই in modern Bengali, but historically longer. Think of the curl at the top like stretching the 'ee' sound — though today both are spoken identically.

letters.name: hrôshsho u (short u)
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'u' in 'put' or 'pull'. A short, rounded 'oo' — purse your lips like you're saying 'oo' but keep it brief.

letters.name: dirghô u (long u)
letters.memoryTrick: Same sound as short উ in modern Bengali, but historically longer. Think of the curl underneath like stretching the 'oo' — though spoken identically to short u today.

letters.name: ri (vocalic r)
letters.memoryTrick: Pronounced 'ri' as in 'river' in modern Bengali, not the ancient Sanskrit vocalic 'r'. Think of the curl underneath as a tiny 'r' tucked under a vowel.

letters.name: e
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'e' in 'bed' or sometimes 'a' in 'cat' — a short, open 'eh'. The horizontal line on top is the headstroke (matra) common to most Bengali letters.

letters.name: oi
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'oi' in 'oil' or 'oy' in 'boy' — a diphthong that glides from 'o' to 'i'. Can also sound closer to 'e' in some modern Bengali speech.

letters.name: o
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'o' in 'go' or 'no' — a clear, rounded 'oh'. Also serves as the word for 'and' in Bengali.

letters.name: ou
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ow' in 'low' or 'o' in 'go' with a slight 'u' at the end — a diphthong. Think of it as ও with an extra curl underneath.

letters.name: kô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'k' in 'kite'. The first consonant of the Bengali alphabet — crisp and unaspirated. Think of a clean, sharp knock on a door.

letters.name: khô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'kh' in 'blockhead' — an aspirated 'k' with a puff of air. Put your hand in front of your mouth; you should feel the burst of breath.

letters.name: gô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'g' in 'go'. A voiced, unaspirated sound — your vocal cords vibrate. Think of a gentle, soft 'guh'.

letters.name: ghô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'gh' in 'doghouse' — a voiced, aspirated 'g' with a breathy release. Your throat should vibrate while air rushes out.

letters.name: ngô (ungô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ng' in 'sing'. This letter never appears at the start of Bengali words — it only appears in the middle or end, often as part of a conjunct. Think of the nasal hum at the end of 'song'.

letters.name: cô (chô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ch' in 'chat' or 'church'. A crisp, unaspirated palatal sound made with the tongue touching the roof of your mouth.

letters.name: chô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'chh' in 'itch-house' — an aspirated 'ch' with a strong puff of air. Think of a sneeze: 'achhoo!' has the same breathy feel.

letters.name: jô (bôrgiyô jô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'j' in 'jam' or 'jump'. A voiced palatal sound with vocal cord vibration. In Eastern Bengal and Bangladesh it can sound closer to 'z' in 'zebra'.

letters.name: jhô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'jh' in 'hedgehog' — a voiced, aspirated 'j' with a breathy buzz. Your vocal cords vibrate while air hisses through your mouth.

letters.name: ñô (iyô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'n' in 'canyon' — a palatal nasal. Almost never appears word-initially in native Bengali; it's famous as part of the common conjunct 'জ্ঞ' (jñô). Think of the Spanish ñ.

letters.name: ṭô (murdhônyô ṭô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a hard 't' pronounced with the tongue curled back to the roof of your mouth — retroflex. Think of the way some Indian English speakers say 'train' with a firm, rolled-back 't'.

letters.name: ṭhô (murdhônyô ṭhô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a hard, aspirated retroflex 't' — the tongue curls back and a puff of air follows. Think of saying 't-hut' with your tongue curled way back.

letters.name: ḍô (murdhônyô ḍô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a hard, retroflex 'd' — tongue curled back, vocal cords buzzing. Think of the firm 'd' in how some English speakers say 'drum'.

letters.name: ḍhô (murdhônyô ḍhô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a hard, breathy retroflex 'd' — tongue curled back, voice buzzing, with a puff of air. Think of saying 'd-hum' with your tongue curled far back.

letters.name: ṇô (murdhônyô ṇô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a retroflex 'n' — tongue curled way back, nasal sound vibrating in your nose. Primarily used in tatsama (Sanskrit-derived) words. Rarely word-initial.

letters.name: tô (dôntyô tô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a soft dental 't' — tongue touches the back of your upper teeth, not the roof of your mouth. Think of the gentle 't' in French 'tu' or Spanish 'tú'.

letters.name: thô (dôntyô thô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a soft, aspirated dental 't' — tongue on teeth with a puff of air. Think of saying 't-humb' with your tongue touching your teeth.

letters.name: dô (dôntyô dô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a soft dental 'd' — tongue touches the back of your upper teeth, voice buzzing. Think of the gentle 'd' in Spanish 'dedo'.

letters.name: dhô (dôntyô dhô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a soft, breathy dental 'd' — tongue on teeth, voice buzzing, with air flowing through. Think of 'd-huh' said with your tongue touching your teeth.

letters.name: nô (dôntyô nô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'n' in 'no'. A dental nasal — tongue touches the back of your upper teeth. This is the most common 'n' in Bengali, appearing in everyday words.

letters.name: pô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'p' in 'pen'. A clean, unaspirated lip sound — no puff of air. Think of a light pop of the lips.

letters.name: phô
letters.memoryTrick: In standard Bengali it's an aspirated 'p' like 'ph' in 'uphill' — a puff of air after the 'p'. In Eastern dialects and Bangladesh, it's often pronounced like English 'f' in 'fan'.

letters.name: bô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'b' in 'boy'. A voiced, unaspirated lip sound. In some positions (especially between vowels) it can soften to a 'v'-like sound in Eastern dialects.

letters.name: bhô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'bh' in 'clubhouse' — a voiced, breathy 'b'. In many modern Bengali dialects it's become a soft, airy 'v'-like sound, especially in Eastern Bengal.

letters.name: mô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'm' in 'mom'. Hum through your nose with your lips together. Think of the satisfied 'mmm' sound when eating something delicious.

letters.name: jô (ôntôsthô jô)
letters.memoryTrick: In standard Bengali, pronounced like 'j' in 'jam' (identical to জ in speech). Historically a 'y' sound, and it still behaves like 'y' in conjuncts (e.g. স + য = স্য 'sy'). Think of it as the 'y' letter that learned to say 'j'.

letters.name: rô
letters.memoryTrick: Like a tapped or trilled 'r' as in Spanish 'pero'. The tongue taps the roof of the mouth once or twice. Think of a quick drum roll — shorter than the rolled Scottish 'r'.

letters.name: lô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'l' in 'lamp'. The tongue touches the roof of the mouth right behind the teeth. Think of the smooth, liquid sound of water lapping.

letters.name: śô (talôbyô śô)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'sh' in 'shoe' or 'ship' — a palatal sibilant. Think of telling someone to be quiet: 'shhh'. Identical in pronunciation to ষ and স in most modern Bengali.

letters.name: ṣô (murdhônyô ṣô)
letters.memoryTrick: Historically a retroflex 'sh', but in modern Bengali it's pronounced exactly like শ and স — all are plain 'sh'. Think of it as the 'retroflex sh' that lost its curl and now sounds just like the others.

letters.name: sô (dôntyô sô)
letters.memoryTrick: In modern standard Bengali, pronounced as 'sh' like শ — but historically and in some dialects a dental 's' like in English 'sun'. Think of it as the most common 'sh' letter — it starts more words than any other sibilant.

letters.name: hô
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'h' in 'hat'. In Bengali it can be voiced — a breathy 'h' with vibration in your throat, like a gentle sigh. Think of the soft exhale when you fog up a mirror.

letters.name: yô (ôntôsthô ẏô, y with nuqta)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'y' in 'yes' — the true 'y' sound of Bengali. Think of it as য with a dot underneath that says 'remember — I'm the real y-sound, not a j-sound!'

letters.name: ṛô (ḍô with nuqta)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a flapped 'r' as in the American English 'butter' or 'ladder' — the tongue flicks once against the roof of the mouth. Think of ড with a dot that softens it into a quick tap.

letters.name: ṛhô (ḍhô with nuqta)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a breathy, flapped 'rh' — a quick retroflex tap with air flowing through. Think of ঢ with a softening dot: the heavy breath of ঢ turns into a lighter, flapped sound.

letters.name: khôndô tô (broken ta)
letters.memoryTrick: Like a dental 't' without the built-in vowel — a bare 't' sound. Think of it as half a ত (tô), like cutting the letter in half. Used at the end of words where no vowel follows.

letters.name: a-kar (vowel sign aa)
letters.memoryTrick: The vowel sign for আ (long a). Written as a vertical line after the consonant. Think of it as stretching the inherent 'ô' into a long 'ah' — like ক + া = কা (ka).

letters.name: i-kar (hrôshsho i-kar)
letters.memoryTrick: The vowel sign for short ই. Written as a small curl BEFORE the consonant but pronounced after it. Think of it as reaching forward: even though the mark comes first in writing, you say the vowel after — ক + ি = কি (ki).

letters.name: ii-kar (dirghô i-kar)
letters.memoryTrick: The vowel sign for long ঈ. Written as a curl after the consonant, with a decorative tail. Looks like the short i-kar with a little extra flourish — ক + ী = কী (kī). Same sound as short i in modern Bengali.

letters.name: u-kar (hrôshsho u-kar)
letters.memoryTrick: The vowel sign for short উ. Written as a small curl BELOW the consonant. Think of it curling downward like a little hook pulling the sound down — ক + ু = কু (ku).

letters.name: uu-kar (dirghô u-kar)
letters.memoryTrick: The vowel sign for long ঊ. Written as a curl below with a little hook at the end. Like the short u-kar with a small extra tail — ক + ূ = কূ (kū). Same sound as short u in modern Bengali.

letters.name: ri-kar (vowel sign ri)
letters.memoryTrick: The vowel sign for ঋ. Written as a small curl below with a flick to the right. Think of it as a tiny 'r' tucked under the consonant — ক + ৃ = কৃ (kri).

letters.name: e-kar (vowel sign e)
letters.memoryTrick: The vowel sign for এ. Written as a slanted curl BEFORE the consonant but pronounced after — another 'reach-back' mark. ক + ে = কে (ke). Think of it leaning forward from the left.

letters.name: oi-kar (vowel sign oi)
letters.memoryTrick: The vowel sign for ঐ. Written as a slanted curl with a small flourish before the consonant. Looks like the e-kar with an extra flick — ক + ৈ = কৈ (koi). Think 'e-kar plus a twist equals oi'.

letters.name: o-kar (vowel sign o)
letters.memoryTrick: The vowel sign for ও. Written as a combination: the e-kar on the left AND the a-kar on the right. ক + ো = কো (ko). Think of it as wrapping the consonant: e-kar before + a-kar after = the round 'o' sound.

letters.name: ou-kar (vowel sign ou)
letters.memoryTrick: The vowel sign for ঔ. Written as the oi-kar on the left AND a-kar on the right. ক + ৌ = কৌ (kou). Like the o-kar but with the oi-kar curve replacing the e-kar — wrapping the consonant in a two-sided embrace.

letters.name: ônusśar (anusvara)
letters.memoryTrick: The anusvara — a dot above a consonant that adds a nasal 'ng' sound. Think of it as closing your nose at the end of a syllable, like the 'ng' in 'song'. Also called 'bindu' (dot) in poetry.

letters.name: bisôrgô (visarga)
letters.memoryTrick: The visarga — two dots that add a breathy 'h' release at the end of a syllable. Think of it as exhaling softly after the sound, like a gentle sigh. Rare in everyday Bengali; mostly in Sanskrit-origin words.

letters.name: côndrôbindu (chandrabindu)
letters.memoryTrick: The chandrabindu ('moon-dot') — a curved mark above a letter that nasalizes the vowel. Think of it as humming through your nose while saying the vowel, like the French 'bon' or Portuguese 'não'.

letters.name: hôsôntô (hasanta / virama)
letters.memoryTrick: The hasanta — a small diagonal stroke below a consonant that removes its inherent vowel. Think of it as the 'vowel killer' or 'mute button': ক is 'kô', but ক্ is just 'k'. It's how Bengali forms consonant clusters.
